source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 22 April 1927, p. 12 ("Tyrone nominations: Dungannon Board of Guardians contests"); Northern Whig, 22 April 1927, p. 5 ("Dungannon Rural Council and Board of Guardians")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: nominations read on the block images of the Belfast News-Letter (22 April 1927, p. 12, article BNL19270422.2.236), labels as printed; one nomination in each division listed, so each was returned unopposed (the contests reported are for the Board of Guardians' urban wards only); the Northern Whig of the same day (image read, council-audit Nov 2026) prints "Altmore—Mr. John Fox (N.)", the form of the 1930 return; the News-Letter's "Foy" is a misprint

note: Triennial election of the Dungannon rural district councillors, 1927. The Belfast News-Letter of 22 April 1927, p. 12, prints one nomination for each of eighteen divisions; Minterburn is not in the list and is not recorded. No poll was held for the rural council; Tyrone's polling day was Wednesday 1 June 1927. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Corrected from the page images of Belfast News-Letter, 22 April 1927, p. 12 and Northern Whig, 22 April 1927, p. 5 (council-audit, Nov 2026): John Foy -> John Fox; the News-Letter prints "Foy", the Northern Whig and the 1930 return "Fox".
